clauses.current_legal_basis: The held original (31 FR 10603) states no end for the delegation or the saving provision. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order in a note at 22 U.S.C. 211a, set out with no ending statement, and 22 U.S.C. 211a, held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t22-s211a.txt, still lets the Secretary of State grant, issue and verify passports under such rules as the President shall designate and prescribe. The eCFR (as of 2026-10-14) lists E.O. 11295 (31 FR 10603) in the authority lines of 22 CFR part 22 and 22 CFR part 51. Executive Order 14348 (90 FR 43895, September 5, 2025) section 3(d) cites the order as a current basis for passport travel restrictions. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The recital cites 3 U.S.C. 301 and the President's authority, and section 1 designates and empowers the Secretary of State to exercise, without the approval, ratification or other action of the President, the authority conferred on the President by the first section of the Act of July 3, 1926 (22 U.S.C. 211a) to designate and prescribe rules governing the granting, issuing and verifying of passports. The delegation states no duration, date or condition that ends it. The held 22 U.S.C. 211a and 3 U.S.C. 301 are in force, the U.S. Code note and the authority lines of 22 CFR parts 22 and 51 still cite the order, Executive Order 14348 (2025) relies on it, and no held instrument revokes or supersedes it, so section 1 is operative on 2026-10-14.

The introductory line of section 2 provides that, subject to section 3, the orders listed after it are hereby superseded. It is a one-time command whose effect is complete on issuance: by its own terms, the superseding took effect on the order's date of August 5, 1966, so this clause ended on 1966-08-05 by performance, with the listed orders' rules preserved only through section 3.

Section 2(1) supersedes Executive Order No. 7856 of March 31, 1938, Rules Governing the Granting and Issuing of Passports in the United States. The supersession is a one-time command performed on issuance, so the clause ended on 1966-08-05 by its own terms; rules in that order in force on that date survive only under the saving provision in section 3.

Section 2(2) supersedes Executive Order No. 8820 of July 11, 1941, Amending the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States. The supersession is a one-time command performed on issuance, so the clause ended on 1966-08-05 by its own terms; rules in that order in force on that date survive only under the saving provision in section 3.

clauses.reason: Section 3 keeps the rules and regulations in the superseded orders, and those issued under them, in force on the order's date in full force and effect until revoked, or except as amended or modified in pursuance of the authority conferred by this order, unless sooner terminated by operation of law. It states no date; it lasts as long as the rules remain unrevoked, and the current Department of State passport regulations (22 CFR parts 22 and 51) cite the order as authority. No held source shows the saved rules revoked as a whole or the saving provision ended, so it is treated as operative on 2026-10-14, with the limitation that no particular saved rule is identified.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (31 FR 10603, signed 1966-08-05; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11295.txt): under 3 U.S.C. 301 and the President's authority, section 1 designates and empowers the Secretary of State to exercise, without further presidential action, the authority conferred on the President by the first section of the Act of July 3, 1926 (22 U.S.C. 211a) to designate and prescribe rules governing the granting, issuing and verifying of passports; section 2 supersedes Executive Order 7856 of March 31, 1938 and Executive Order 8820 of July 11, 1941, subject to section 3; section 3 saves the rules and regulations in those orders, and those issued under them, in force when the order was issued until revoked or amended in pursuance of the authority conferred by this order, unless sooner terminated by operation of law. The dossier inventory omitted the recital and section 1, so it is corrected with inventory overrides (five clauses covering the whole text). The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 2 hits: the Office of the Federal Register note 'Provisionally supersedes: EO 7856, EO 8820' (the order's own effect on earlier orders) and a see-reference to 55 FR 3676 and Executive Order 14348 (September 5, 2025). The held text of Executive Order 14348 (90 FR 43895) mentions this order only as one basis for geographic passport restrictions in its section 3(d); it does not amend, revoke or supersede it. current-law:usc has 3 hits: the 22 U.S.C. 211a note prints the order with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 3 hits: 22 CFR parts 22 and 51 cite the order in their authority lines. The authority statutes are checked: 3 U.S.C. 301 (held, jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t3-s301.txt) and 22 U.S.C. 211a (held) are both in the U.S. Code and still authorize the delegation. The held-corpus search for the number 11295 found no revocation or supersession.

savings.reason: Section 3 saves the rules and regulations contained in the superseded Executive Orders 7856 and 8820 and those issued under them that were in force on 1966-08-05, continuing until revoked or amended under the authority conferred by this order unless terminated by operation of law. The held current regulations (22 CFR parts 22 and 51) cite this order as authority, so the passport rule-making continues under section 1; no held source shows a particular saved rule still in force or ended, so the saved rules are treated as continuing under section 3 and as carried into the Department of State regulations.
